newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK OIL REFINERIES 96 SALES UP 31PCT TO 920BLN DRS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK OIL REFINERIES 96 SALES UP 31PCT TO 920BLN DRS.

text.p: The sales of Greece's four oil refineries rose 31 percent to 920 billion drachmas in 1996 from 700 billion in 1995 on the back of higher international oil prices and output, said private MultiPress in a statement.

"Total sales of the three companies that control two state and two private refineries -- Public Petroleum Corporation (DEP), Motor Oil Hellas and Petrola Hellas -- rose 31 percent or 220 billion drachmas to 920 billion in 1996," it said.

Sales of private Motor Oil Hellas rose 32 percent or 58.6 billion to 239.1 billion drachmas in 1996, helping it return to the black with profits of about 1.0 billion drachmas after losses of 2.46 billion in 1995, it said.
Saudi Aramco bought a 50 percent stake in Motor Oil Hellas from the Vardinoyiannis family in March 1996 which retains a 50 percent stake in the company.
Sales of private Petrola Hellas which belongs to the Latsis group rose 35.5 percent or 56.7 billion to 216.2 billion drachmas, it added.
Petrola Hellas cut its losses by 65 percent to 714 million drachmas in 1996 despite high exceptional non-operating expenses, the statement said.

Output from the two state oil refineries stood at 383 billion drachmas in 1996 of which 273 billion drachmas came from the Hellenic Refineries at Aspropyrgos (ELDA) and the rest from the EKO refineries.
ELDA's profits exceeded 15 billion drachmas in 1996 from 7.4 billion in 1995, posting the biggest increase among Greek industrial firms in 1996, it said.

All figures come from Multipress CD-ROM "Greek Greek industry and Economy" which reviews developments in the largest 1,200 Greek industrial companies in 1996. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
